Validate value ranges

Source: R/data_quality.R
validate_ranges.Rd

Check that the data respect basic business rules and remove invalid rows. The rules include: strictly positive salary, remote work ratio between 0 and 100, and a plausible work year.

Usage

validate_ranges(
  data,
  min_year = 2000,
  max_year = as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y"))
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame containing the salary, remote_ratio and work_year columns.

min_year

Integer. Minimum acceptable year (default 2000).

max_year

Integer. Maximum acceptable year (default: current system year).

Value

A filtered data.frame (the number of rows may be lower than the original).

Details

This function applies a strict filter. A row is kept only if all of the following conditions are TRUE:

  • salary > 0

  • remote_ratio is between 0 and 100 inclusive

  • work_year is between min_year and max_year

  • none of these values is NA

A message is printed to the console if some rows are removed.

See also

Other Data quality: cap_outliers_salary()

Examples

# Data with an invalid row (negative salary and remote_ratio > 100)
df <- data.frame(
  salary = c(50000, -100, 60000),
  remote_ratio = c(50, 150, 100),
  work_year = c(2022, 2022, 2023)
)

# Apply the filter
df_clean <- validate_ranges(df)
#> Error in validate_ranges(df): could not find function "validate_ranges"

# Result: only valid rows are kept
nrow(df_clean) # Should be 2
#> Error: object 'df_clean' not found
